mechanism_narrative: The observed four-week upward trend in RETAIL_REC, indicating a gradual return to pre-pandemic activity levels, will continue to drive further increases in retail and recreation mobility over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days, despite the preceding upward trend.

mechanism_narrative: The sustained improvement in WORKPLACES mobility, consistently remaining above -10% for the last two weeks, signifies a solid return to office-based routines that will directly increase retail and recreation activity during weekdays over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES consistently above -10% for two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days does not increase, or decreases, despite WORKPLACES remaining above -10%.

mechanism_narrative: The combined trend of decreasing RESIDENTIAL mobility and increasing TRANSIT station mobility indicates a growing willingness among the population to spend time outside their homes and utilize public transport, which will positively impact retail and recreation over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days decreases, even if RESIDENTIAL continues to fall and TRANSIT continues to rise.

mechanism_narrative: The significant week-on-week rebound in PARKS mobility from t-1w to t-0w suggests a broader increase in outdoor activity and public engagement, which will spill over into higher retail and recreation mobility over the next four weeks as people extend their outings.
candidate_trigger: PARKS increases by more than 5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the previous 28 days, despite the observed PARKS rebound.

mechanism_narrative: The consistently high and recently increasing GROCERY_PHARM mobility reflects robust essential consumer activity and general population movement, which serves as a leading indicator for a positive spillover into non-essential retail and recreation within the next week.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days is lower than the average of the last 7 days, despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining high or increasing.

mechanism_narrative: If the upward trend in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility stagnates, failing to improve by at least 1 percentage point week-on-week for two consecutive weeks, it will signal a pause in the return to normal commuting patterns, leading to a negative impact on retail and recreation over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES or TRANSIT fails to improve by 1 point WoW for 2 consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days increases, even if WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility stagnate as described.

mechanism_narrative: The recent rebound in PARKS mobility, combined with the general upward trend in RETAIL_REC, indicates an early seasonal shift towards warmer weather, encouraging more outdoor and out-of-home activities that will further boost retail and recreation over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days decreases, despite the PARKS rebound and the onset of spring.

mechanism_narrative: The sustained low levels of RESIDENTIAL mobility (below 8%) coupled with the continued improvement in WORKPLACES mobility (above -10%) signifies a fundamental shift in daily routines away from home and towards public and commercial spaces, directly boosting retail and recreation over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains below 8% and WORKPLACES remains above -10%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days decreases, even if RESIDENTIAL remains below 8% and WORKPLACES remains above -10%.
